notes: Identity checked independently from the supplied text: title What Counts as a Choice? U.S. Americans Are More Likely Than Indians to Construe Actions as Choices; authors Krishna Savani, Hazel Rose Markus, N.V.R. Naidu, Satishchandra Kumar, and Neha Berlia; DOI 10.1177/0956797609359908; Psychological Science 21(3), 391–398 (2010). This is the primary research article, with five studies, methods, results, figures, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned original-side fields were examined; other fields are placeholders. Study 5 prints culture, condition, and Culture × Condition HLM tests on p. 396; Figure 4 alone does not select among them. The 90 American and 128 Indian participants are method counts, not explicitly final model groups. No analytic N is derived, and no N is inferred from the printed degrees of freedom. Repeated action observations and participants remain distinct roles.
